intent:
"yes approbe and begin the implementation" started the bstack build slice by slice, strictly one at a time ("keep it sequential"). Later: "i'm only not concerned about security hardening, threat-model concerns. Style and simplification and following proper design principles are still important." - build the full app fast, but review the core properly so slices and phases do not leave bugs.

The plans of record are in the repo: `docs/design.md` (requirements and decisions, including R24: licensing is out of scope, and the approved baseline rule: at least three realistic comparable scenarios, no failure quota) and `docs/implementation-plan.md` (tasks, task evidence contract). knowttl/bstack is public, has no GitHub Actions or workflows and no release automation, and ships through the no-mistakes pipeline (`.no-mistakes.yaml` owns the review budget and focus) with automatic merge of green work. Landed: Phase 0, T1.1 and C7a (https://github.com/knowttl/bstack/pull/14: acceptance registry, scenarios, run records and manual scoring).

This piece is slice C7b, the rest of task T1.2: one current-host adapter, isolation and the recorded baseline (slice done evidence: fresh sessions, no-skill discovery absence, unique transcripts, comparable model, revision and criteria).

for each evaluation run, copy ONLY the existing Codex login file (the auth file in the invoking user's CODEX_HOME) into a fresh throwaway isolated CODEX_HOME created for that run with mode 0700 (file 0600), containing no skills, config or other state; run the session; delete that isolated home immediately after the run, including on failure or timeout. Never print, log, record in evidence, or commit the credential or its contents; record only that the run authenticated via a throwaway copy. Verify isolation (no repo-audit skill discoverable in without mode) before scoring.

The captain approved copying only the invoking user's Codex login into throwaway state with private permissions. The implementation removes the login after each turn and the entire isolated home on conversation close or failure.

Historical C7b publication review retained from the landed commit: redacted identities, unchanged baseline verdicts, provenance, transcript hashes and citation bounds. The refreshed evaluation suite covers archived-evidence consumers, not a new live session.

limitations: Live baseline used Codex CLI 0.160.1, gpt-6.1-sol, Node 24 and Linux only. It does not prove Windows or macOS support, an agent/model matrix, or final released-skill acceptance.

Host question matching is reviewer-driven. Scripted answers are sent through resumed host turns only for corresponding questions. New-idea and clear-goals asked no questions, so no extra scripted replies were invented.

New-idea skipped the intent interview, included browser local storage in its domain terms, and declared the generated VISION approved without scripted user approval. Its actual failed result and generated VISION remain evidence.

Clear-goals reused its approved documents. Its host trace includes a broad parent-directory filename search interrupted by the host, followed by recommendations based on the fixture documents. This observation is retained without adding a scoring criterion.
The 75 registry definitions remain planned until their owning tasks register completed procedures. Registry validation does not pass acceptance cases.

Fake host and dummy-login tests verify the command boundary and cleanup, not model interpretation. Published model output is redacted for host metadata while retaining scored observations and line citations.

All live isolated homes, authentication copies and fixtures were removed after their outputs were preserved. Closed runs retain verified discovery inventory and a bound conversation hash for later scoring.

This review changes lifecycle entry points and published evidence representations without rerunning live models or handling credentials. Raw host sessions cannot be resumed from redacted archival identifiers. Full local validation now passes on the landed C7b commit.
